newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Metals-Aluminium demand slows, zinc to Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Asia Metals-Aluminium demand slows, zinc to Singapore.

text.p: Asian demand for aluminium has slowed with the exception of Japan while some 5,000 tonnes of zinc will arrive in Singapore from China for re-sale to take advantage of high prices, traders said on Friday.
"Demand for aluminium has slackened around the region. But Japanese demand has even strengthened with premiums going up," an aluminium dealer for a European metal trading company told Reuters.
Japanese premiums were being quoted by the trade at US$90 a tonne CIF over cash LME prices against a quote last week of $80-$82 a tonne on the same basis.
"The premiums traded have moved higher. There's still probably some demand in Japan," trader for a metal dealing company said.

"Japanese aluminium demand is very strong. They're buying a lot of material," the general manager of a Japanese metal trading company in Singapore said. Most of the purchases were being made by the Japanese car industry, he added.
Traders said up to 8,000 tonnes of aluminium seemed to have been shipped out of warehouses in Singapore, but they were unsure whether it would wind up in Japan.
"If Japan really needs the material, I guess they can ship it directly there. We're just not sure where the material is going to," one dealer said.
Indonesian buying, however, has slowed after several companies completed acquisitions after failing to sign long-term supply contracts for the second quarter of 1997, dealers said.
"People who don't need aluminium soon are now holding back and hoping for lower premiums," a dealer said.
The aluminium in the LME's Singapore warehouse reached 17,325 tonnes in the LME stocks report last Tuesday, down 125 tonnes from the previous report last Friday.
Far East dealers said aluminium prices in the LME may make a stab at $1,680 a tonne after closing on Thursday at $1,669.
"But we'll probably see good selling as early as $1,670 to $1,675 and this may push the price down to around $1,630 (a tonne)," a trader said.
Three-month aluminium was being quoted by Singapore-based dealers at 0700 GMT at $1,665/70 a tonne.
On the other hand, about 5,000 tonnes of zinc from China will arrive in Singapore over the next few days for possible re-sale to take advantage of the recent surge in LME zinc prices, traders said.
"I think about half of that zinc will be placed on warrant at the LME warehouse here," a dealer for a Japanese trading house said.
"The Chinese are selling a lot," a European metal dealer said.
Traders said zinc still had the strength to punch higher on the LME after closing on Thursday $9 up on the day at $1,305 a tonne.
"I think zinc can rise to as high as $1,320 (a tonne) before we see good profit-taking," a Japanese trader said.
"Next resistance is seen around $1,325-$1,330," metal brokers Brandeis said in its daily review.
But another trader said zinc may run out of steam soon, especially with copper and aluminium range-bound in the LME.
"There may be a big drop in zinc soon. It may hold this position for a while, but I don't think it can last with copper and aluminium having a difficult time," he said.
Copper trading in the region remained subdued with no signs of China in the market, traders said.
Three-month copper was seen by the trade at 0700 GMT at around $2,357/62 a tonne, unchanged from the late quote in London on Thursday.
